Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the ElectroDrive Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to ElectroDrive Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hale, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Mike Torres, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Lena Novak, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 was a significant quarter for ElectroDrive Motors, marked by progress across our key strategic initiatives. We achieved notable milestones in battery cost reductions per kWh, changes in our order backlog and reservation trends, gross margin improvements with solid guidance, average selling price trends across models and regions, managing impacts from raw material costs and supply chain disruptions, and ramping production volumes alongside capacity utilization rates. We are particularly pleased with the initial customer response to our new Forge truck, and its contribution to our backlog is substantial.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, our revenue reached $2.85 billion, demonstrating a 32% increase compared to the same period last year. Our gross margin stood at 22.1%, reflecting our commitment to operational excellence. Operating expenses amounted to $520 million, and net income was $185 million. We maintain a robust financial position with $4.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our outlook for the upcoming quarter is strong, with expected revenue of $3.2 to $3.4 billion and continued margin expansion.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here, the energy feels like midday progress. Before we move on, let me dive deep into some pivotal elements shaping our results, starting with one of the most critical cost levers in our EV business: battery costs per kWh. Batteries make up about 35-40% of our bill of materials for flagship models like the Horizon SUV and Bolt-X sedan, so every dollar counts for margins and pricing power. In Q3, our average lithium-ion battery cell cost hit $82 per kWh, down 18% year-over-year from $100 per kWh in Q3 2023 and 5% sequentially from Q2's $86 per kWh. At the pack level—including modules, battery management systems, cooling, and structural integration—we're at $105 per kWh, a 16% YoY drop from $125 per kWh. These numbers cover our main chemistries: NMC 811 for the high-performance Horizon packs at 250 Wh/kg energy density, and LFP for the cost-effective Bolt-X at 190 Wh/kg with over 3,000 cycles at 80% capacity retention.

This tracks BloombergNEF's global pack average of $112 per kWh for 2024—we're 6% ahead thanks to vertical integration and smart supplier choices. For comparison, Tesla's implied cell costs hover at $75-80 per kWh with their 4680 ramp, and BYD's Blade LFP is sub-$60 per kWh at scale. We're competitive in premium EVs with room to push toward mass-market levels. Driving this are massive scale effects—global cell production reached 1.2 TWh annualized, up 40% YoY per Rho Motion—and innovations like shifting to LFP for 45% of packs, up from 25% last year, using CATL's Shenxing and Qilin CTP 2.0 at $65 per kWh versus $95 for NMC, avoiding cobalt and nickel amid China's 25% LFP market surge.

Manufacturing advances include dry electrode coating at our Nevada Gigafactory 2, cutting slurry drying costs 20-30% with 15% pilot yields aiming for 50% by mid-2025, potentially saving $10-15 per kWh. We're shifting 30% of Horizon packs to 46-series cylindrical cells from prismatic, hitting 280 Wh/kg like Panasonic's 4680 at 90%+ yields. Regionally, China's $70-85 per kWh packs from CATL and BYD's 60% market dominance get us $78 per kWh landed via their Hungary plant, sidestepping full US tariffs. North America's IRA packs from LG's Arizona line cost $110 per kWh but snag the full $45 per kWh credit—a 40% subsidy. Europe trails at $120 per kWh with labor and CBAM taxes hitting Northvolt hard, while Korea's SK On and Samsung SDI sit at $95 per kWh under IRA pressures.

We're proactive: our Texas in-house gigafactory ramps to 40 GWh/year by 2026, internalizing 25% supply at $60 per kWh targeted via LFP/NMC hybrids and sodium-ion R&D for $50 per kWh at 160 Wh/kg by 2028. Our Redwood JV recycled 5 GWh black mass in Q3, recovering 95% lithium worth $5 per kWh equivalent, offsetting 8% of virgin costs. We see cell costs at $65 per kWh by end-2025 and $55 by 2027, faster than BNEF's 15% CAGR. For a 75 kWh pack, $10 per kWh savings equals $1,500 BOM reduction, enabling $2,000 ASP cuts or 200 bps margin gains. We've passed 60% savings to customers—Horizon pricing down 12% YoY—driving 25% US share gains against BYD imports. Batteries are our tailwind, positioning us for 28% gross margins in 2025 ahead of legacy OEMs at $130+ per kWh.

Shifting to order backlog and reservation trends, these give us clear visibility into revenue amid high rates and softening sentiment. Our global backlog ended Q3 at $18.7 billion, or 142,000 deposit-secured vehicles at $132,000 ASP—up 12% QoQ from $16.7 billion and 28% YoY from $14.6 billion. Reservations topped 215,000, up 18% QoQ and 35% YoY, net of cancellations. Backlog converts at 85% over 12 months, beating peers like Rivian and Lucid at 70-75%, thanks to configurator ordering.

By product, Horizon SUV drives 62% of backlog—88,000 units at $12.1 billion, $137,500 ASP—boosted by the Long Range variant's 120 kWh pack for 520-mile range. Bolt-X is 28% at 40,000 units, $4.2 billion, aided by IRA pricing. Forge truck added 14,000 reservations worth $2.4 billion since launch, with 800V for 350 kW charging. Net Q3 reservations grew 42,000, up 25% QoQ via "Reserve Now, Drive Later" for Highway Autonomy. Cancellations rose to 4.2% from financing, but below industry 8-10%.

North America is 68% ($12.7 billion, +15% QoQ) via Spartanburg at 95% utilization. Europe 22% ($4.1 billion) strong in UK/Germany with Bolt-X's 480 km WLTP. China 7% ($1.3 billion) dipped 8% QoQ but Shanghai localization targets reversal. Asia ex-China grows with Forge. Drivers: 60-day fulfillment from cell integration, 85 GWh supply lock-ins, ElectraOS 2.0 OTA for 7% efficiency, and 2% ASP compression. We guide $22-25 billion year-end backlog with Forge ramps.

On gross margins, we hit 21.2%—up 450 bps YoY, 120 bps QoQ—from Nevada at 1.2 GWh, 65% high-margin Horizon mix, and 4680 cells at $92 per kWh pack. FY2024 guide 22.5-24.0%, Q4 high end; FY2025 25-27% to match Tesla. Assumptions: 285,000-305,000 deliveries (+35% YoY), Q4 85,000 at 85% utilization absorbing $450 million fixed costs via structural packs. ASP $52,000-54,000 flat-up 2% on 40% premium mix, software at 18% attach. COGS $38,000-40,000 (-12% YoY): batteries $110/kWh with dry coating, SiC inverters, 18% vertical on chassis. FX tailwind 50 bps, $100 million labor savings. Upside from Autonomy V3, risks IRA changes.

ASP trends show blended $52,300, +9% YoY, +2% QoQ. Ex-credits $50,500 (+8%). By model: Spark $38,200 (-5% YoY, +25% volume), Trailblazer $55,400 (flat YoY), Hauler $72,100 (+3%), Apex $110,500 (+12%). Mix added 450 bps. Regions: NA $60,200 (+12%, IRA), Europe $50,800 (+5%), China $45,100 (-2%), ROW $48,900 (+7%). Content up $4,200 YoY via 4680, unboxed, FSD subs. H2 target $54,500.

Raw materials and disruptions: Metals 45% COGS. Lithium $14,500/ton (-70% peak), nickel $18,000/ton, cobalt $28,000, aluminum $2,800. Inflated packs 18% YoY, margins to 22.4%. Red Sea added 25-30 days, semis cut 2,500 trucks. Mitigations: 20 GWh in-house, 36-month offtakes, LFP-silicon, $500M hedges. Tailwinds to $12,000/ton lithium.

Production: 452,300 units (+28% YoY, +12% QoQ), FY 1.75M. Deliveries 448,700, 1.2 months inventory. Bolt SUV 58%, Spark 22%, Thunder 15%. Utilization 78%: US 82%, China 85%, Europe 72%. Cost $28,400 (-11% YoY), margins 21.5%. Gen-3 automation, 45% in-house cells. Q4 480-500k at 80-83%.

Next, I'll hand the call over to Mike Torres for an update on our manufacturing operations.

Mike Torres:
Thank you, Sarah. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at peak efficiency to meet the growing demand for our vehicles. Building on the production volumes and 78% utilization Sarah detailed, we've implemented lean principles like Gen-3 automation and unboxed processes across our Gigafactories, improving throughput by 15% and cutting scrap under 1%. We've reduced lead times to under 60 days through vertical integration on 4680 cells supplying 45% of packs. We're confident in scaling to 85-90% utilization as we add capacity in Texas and India.

Following me, Dr. Lena Novak will provide insights into our technological advancements.

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thank you. We continue to invest heavily in research and development to maintain our technological edge. Our advancements in battery tech—like dry electrode coating and LFP-silicon blends at 320 Wh/kg—and autonomous systems such as Highway Autonomy L3 and ElectraOS 2.0 predictive management position us as a leader. OTA software bundles are boosting ASP by 2-3% and addressing range anxiety with 7% real-world gains.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one.

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. Sarah, can you expand on the backlog trends, especially in China and how localization is helping?

Jordan Hale:
Thanks for the question. As Sarah noted, China backlog dipped 8% QoQ to 7% of total due to local competition like BYD and NIO, but our Shanghai strategy with 40% domestic content by Q4 via CATL LFP unlocks NEV credits. Reservations are accelerating with Forge appeal, and we're seeing conversion strength overall at 85%.

Analyst 2:
Great, thanks. Sarah, on gross margin guidance, what are the biggest risks to the 25-27% FY2025 target?

Sarah Chen:
Key risks are US retail softening from rates—mitigated by 0% APR and IRA rebates—and ASP pressure if Tesla cuts further, but our premium mix and software at $12k FSD-like attach give pricing power. Upside from Autonomy V3 at 25% take-rate adds 200 bps. We're confident with COGS down 12% on batteries and vertical integration.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. Mike, with utilization at 78%, how are disruptions like nickel shortages impacting ramps, and what's the path to 85%?

Mike Torres:
Nickel issues caused brief Shanghai downtime, but diversified offtakes and 45% in-house 4680 cells keep us at 98% on-time delivery. Berlin approvals are resolved; Q4 hits 80-83% with holiday demand and structural packs cutting BoM 8%. Automation unlocks the rest by mid-2025.

Analyst 4:
Appreciate it. Dr. Novak, how do battery trends like sodium-ion factor into your tech roadmap and cost goals?

Dr. Lena Novak:
Sodium-ion R&D targets $50/kWh by 2028 at 160 Wh/kg for urban EVs, complementing LFP/NMC hybrids. Dry coating and 46-series already shave $10-15/kWh, aligning with $65/kWh by 2025. This fuels Horizon's 520-mile range and Forge's 350 kW charging.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Analyst 5:
Hi, team. On ASP by region, how sustainable is the NA premium at $60k with Cybertruck competition?

Jordan Hale:
NA's 12% YoY lift comes from IRA $9,200 average credits and Hauler's 500-mile range towing edge. Mix to premium SUVs/trucks sustains it; software subs add $800 annualized. We're pivoting from low-ASP fleets.

Analyst 6:
Thanks. Sarah, raw materials—lithium stabilizing helps, but what's the disruption risk outlook?

Sarah Chen:
Lithium to $12k/ton by year-end per Fastmarkets; hedges cover 60% Q4-Q1, localization 85% NA by 2026. Red Sea and semis mitigated, positioning 200-300 bps expansion FY25 ahead of peers.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and remain committed to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the ElectroDrive Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
